name: Grunth
summary: In Orgrimmar, Grunth eagerly seeks the company of Horde champions. The young orc lives in the Drag orphanage and, during Children's Week, journeys across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms to learn what it means to be a hero.

sections.title: A Curious Child of the Horde
sections.body: Grunth is a young orc orphan in the Drag of Orgrimmar, where Orphan Matron Battlewail cares for him. Raised in Durotar's harsh red wastes, he watches armored adventurers with awe and asks them questions without end. Are armored warriors truly terrifying? Why does lightning on water not kill every fish? Will he ever see someone fight an actual dragon?

sections.title: Children's Week Journeys
sections.body: During Children's Week, an Orcish Orphan Whistle summons Grunth to travel with adventurers on a tour across the world. He wants to meet High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof in Mulgore, see the ruined throne room of Lordaeron, and visit the rugged frontiers where his people fight for their future.

faq.answer: Grunth is an orc child at the Orgrimmar orphanage in the Drag. Orphan Matron Battlewail cares for him, and he dreams of becoming a legendary hero of the Horde.
Grunth lives with the other orphans in the Drag of Orgrimmar. During Children's Week, an Orcish Orphan Whistle from Orphan Matron Battlewail can summon him anywhere.

faq.q: What places does Grunth want to visit?
faq.answer: Grunth wants to see the great places and figures of the Horde. He asks to visit High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof in Thunder Bluff, see the Ratchet docks, and travel to the ruined throne room of Lordaeron.

faq.q: What kind of personality does Grunth have?
faq.answer: Grunth is loud, curious, and full of imagination. He asks adventurers strange questions, like what “zug zug” means and whether a wingless fly is called a walk, and even mentions shoving a rock up his nose.

angles.text: As a Horde champion, guiding Grunth during Children's Week shows you a generation born into freedom rather than demonic servitude, and what your faction strives to protect.
As an orc, Grunth reflects Durotar's youth, raised with tribal honor and the demands of survival rather than the dark lethargy of the internment camps.
